correctness.rationale: For integers \(n\ge2k\ge4\) and \(0\le L<k\), the eigenvalues are computed through a multiplicity-free harmonic decomposition on \(n-2\) residual coordinates, hypergeometric weights for the two special coordinates, and an explicit rank-one projection. The up/down commutator proves lift norms and dimension. Polynomial degree \(L-t\) determines the scalar boundary eigenvalues \(1\), \(A_{L-1}\), and \(B_L\); a telescoping dimension identity fixes all zeros and the endpoints \(L=0\) and \(B_{k-1}=0\). The self-contained exact-rational checker confirms projector idempotence, a spectral annihilator, and traces of powers 1..\(4\) for \(23\) parameter triples involving 773 matrix rows. Finite tests are corroborative, not exhaustive proof.

originality.rationale: The closest complete-text sources supply Johnson harmonic bases (Dunkl; Scarabotti--Tolli; Filmus) or the Johnson Slepian operator for distance-neighborhood subsystems (Bernard--Crampe--Vinet). Their precise statements do not give or imply by direct specialization the complete two-coordinate-face compressed spectrum: a pair-containing face is not a union of reference-vertex distance shells. Endpoint convolution norms and other spatial concentration operators address different mathematical invariants, not this compressed spectrum. Real searches found no stronger directly covering table or formula; residual historical synonym risk remains.
